title: 2025 AMC 12B Problem 11
statement: Nine athletes, no two of whom are the same height, try out for the basketball team. One at a time, they draw a wristband at random, without replacement, from a bag containing \(3\) blue bands, \(3\) red bands, and \(3\) green bands. They are divided into a blue group, a red group, and a green group. The tallest member of each group is named the group captain. What is the probability that the group captains are the three tallest athletes?

solutions.text:
Each group has \(3\) slots. The three tallest athletes are the captains precisely when they fall into three different groups. Placing them one at a time into the \(9\) slots, the second must avoid the first’s group (\(6\) of the remaining \(8\) slots) and the third must avoid both used groups (\(3\) of the remaining \(7\) slots). The probability is \(\dfrac{6}{8} \cdot \dfrac{3}{7} = \dfrac{9}{28}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The captains are the three tallest exactly when the three tallest land in three different groups
Place the tallest three one at a time; each must avoid the groups already used, whose slots shrink the pool
